body.p: This responds to the Non-Final Office Action dated June 13, 2024.
Claims 1 and 13 are presently amended. Claims 11 and 19 are presently canceled. New
claims 21-22 are presently added. As a result, claims 1-10, 12-18, and 20-22 are now pending in this application.
Applicant respectfully submits that no new matter has been introduced, and that the
amendment is supported by, for example, [0056]-[0057] and FIG. 4 of the Application as filed.

Claims 21-22 are new. Independent claim 21 incorporates the limitations of original claim 1 (except for the "output circuit") and claim 2, and the requirement of the primary pulmonary risk score and the secondary pulmonary risk score each taking a numerical value, as similarly made to claim 1. Applicant believes that no new matter has been introduced in such new claims. Applicant further submits that, for the same reasons set forth below with respect to claim 1 and by incorporating the "physiological event detector circuit" limitation of claim 2 (which is not rejected under § 101), the new claims are patent eligible. Further, for at least the same reasons set forth below with respect to claim 1, the new claims are believed to be patentably distinct over the cited references. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests consideration and allowance of the newly added claims.
In the event that this response does not render all claims allowable, Applicant's

representative, Dan Li, formally requests a further telephonic interview with the Examiner upon receipt of this response, in order to carry out telephonic prosecution of this patent application to mutually facilitate and expedite the examination. Applicant's representative can be reached by telephone at 612-373-6945.
Claims 1, 5-6, 8-13 and 16-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly being
directed to non-statutory subject matter. Applicant has canceled claims 11 and 19, and respectfully traverses the rejection of the rest of the claims under § 101.
As described in the October 2019 Patent Eligibility Guidance Update and consistent with

The October 2019 Patent Eligibility Guidance Update set forth that "first the specification should be evaluated to determine if the disclosure provides sufficient details such that one of ordinary skill in the art would recognize the claimed invention as providing an improvement." October 2019 Patent Eligibility Guidance at p. 12. "[I] f the specification sets forth an improvement in technology, the claim must be evaluated to ensure that the claim itself reflects the disclosed improvement. That is, the claim includes the components or steps of the invention that provide the improvement described in the specification. The claim itself does not need to explicitly recite the improvement described in the specification...." Id. MPEP § 2106.04(d) states that, to evaluate improvements in the functioning of a computer or an improvement to any other technology or technical filed in Step 2A Prong Two, first the specification should be evaluated to determine if the disclosure provides sufficient details such that one of ordinary skill in the art would recognize the claimed invention as providing an improvement. ... Second, if the specification sets forth an improvement in technology, the claim must be evaluated to ensure that the claim itself reflects the disclosed improvement. That is, the claim includes the components or steps of the invention that provide the improvement described in the specification. The claim itself does not need to explicitly recite the improvement described in the specification...." (Emphasis added.)

Here, the pending claims reflect an technological improvement, if not merely in the functioning of a computer, in the technology or technical field of computerized, device-based patient monitoring and pulmonary risk management system. Applicant's specification identifies a challenge in device-based disease management, namely accurate/sensitive and specific detections of certain diseases (e.g., cardiac or pulmonary diseases) and patient overall health status. Applicant's specification then describes a technological solution including, among other things, a composite pulmonary risk score to quantify the risk of future pulmonary disease, using a unique combination

The claimed subject matter enables the above-mentioned technological improvement as described in the specification. For example, claims 1 and 13 each recite calculating a primary pulmonary risk score using the first signal metric, calculating a secondary pulmonary risk score using the second and the third signal metrics, and calculating a composite pulmonary risk score using the primary and the secondary pulmonary risk scores. Claims 1 and 13 thus include the components or steps of the invention that reflect the technological improvement as described in the specification.
For at least the foregoing reasons, the claimed subject matter improves an existing

technology or technical field of device-based patient monitoring and pulmonary risk management system, thereby integrating the alleged exception into a practical application under Step 2A Prong Two. See MPEP § 2106.04(d)(1).
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of such rejection and allowance of claims 1, 5-6, 8-13 and 16-20.
The Rejection of Claims Under ? 112
Claims 1-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite.

In particular, the Office Action asserts that the limitations "the first pulmonary signal metric" and "the second and the third pulmonary signal metrics" in claims 1 and 13 lack antecedent basis. Applicant has amended said limitations to provide proper antecedent basis, and respectfully requests withdrawal of this basis of rejection.
The Rejection of Claims Under ? 102
Claims 1, 5, 12 and 20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a) over Patangay (U.S. 2012/0157799). Applicant respectfully traverses.

Applicant has amended claim 1 to more distinctly recite certain aspects of the present subject matter, including, among other things, primary pulmonary risk score and the secondary pulmonary risk score each taking a numerical value. Applicant's specification, e.g., [ 0075]- [0079] with respect to FIG. 4, describes various methods of calculating the primary and second pulmonary risk scores, including statistical measures such as a central tendency or a variability measure, or a weighted combination of signal metrics, all of which would yield risk score taking numerical values.

The Office Action further asserts that element 450 of Patangay FIG. 4 is equivalent to the composite pulmonary risk score as claimed. (Office Action at 4.) Applicant respectfully disagrees. Element 450 is "a multi-dimensional heart failure decompensation status alert" that includes "separate cardiac output dimension 413, a cardiac filling pressure dimension 423, a thoracic fluid status dimension 433, ... a separate respiratory function dimension 443." (Patangay at [0056].) Clearly, by including all of the cardiac indicators, thoracic fluid indicator, and respiratory function indicators, element 450 is an indicator of heart failure decompensation, not a composite pulmonary

risk score indicating pulmonary risk. Further, because the composite pulmonary risk score is calculated using the primary and the secondary pulmonary risk scores each taking a numerical value, the composite pulmonary risk score also takes a numerical value. Patangay does not appear to teach or suggest that element 450, the "multi-dimensional heart failure decompensation status alert," takes a numerical value.
For at least the above reasons, Patangay fails to disclose each and every claim limitation in claim 1, such that a primafacie case of anticipation has not been established with respect to claim 1.

Claims 5 and 12 are dependent from base claim 1, each include patentable subject matter beyond that recited in the base claim 1, and are believed to be patentable for at least the reasons stated above with respect to claim 1.

Claim 20 is dependent from base claim 13. The Office Action does not reject claim 13 on § 102 or § 103 grounds. However, Applicant has amended claim 13 similarly to claim 1, and respectfully submits that claim 13 is patentable for at least the same reason set forth above with respect to claim 1. Claim 20 is patentable at least by virtue of dependency from base claim 13.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this basis of rejection and allowance of claims 1, 5, 10, 12, and 20.
The Rejection of Claims Under ? 103

Claims 2, 4 and 14 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Patangay in view of Van Oort (U.S. 2008/0183085); Claims 8-9 and 17-18 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Patangay in view ofAn (U.S. 2013/0116578); Claims 3 and 15 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Patangay in view of Van Oort and An; Claims 6-7 and 16 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Patangay in view of Van Oort and further in view of Dumont (U.S. 2014/0243690).
Applicant respectfully traverses the above rejections under § 103. The combination of

Patangay with any of Van Oort, An, or Dumont, as suggested in the Office Action, does not rectify the deficiency of Patangay, as stated above with respect to claims 1 and 13, such that aprimafacie case of obviousness has not been established with respect to said claims because all claimed features have not been disclosed or suggested by the combined references.
Claims 2-4 and 6-9 are dependent from base claim 1. Claims 14-18 are dependent from base claim 13. Such dependent claims each include patentable subject matter beyond that recited in their
respective base claims, and are believed to be patentable for at least the reasons stated above with respect to the base claims.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this basis of rejection and allowance of claims 2-4, 6-9, and 14-18.

All rights to pursue any cancelled claims in a subsequent patent application claiming the benefit of priority of the present patent application, and to request rejoinder of any withdrawn claim, as required by MPEP § 821.04, are likewise reserved.
